items.title: Toric-code edge spins on an oriented cellulation
items.physical_scope: Pure finite-dimensional mathematics; no physical premise, empirical claim, or stability claim.
items.statement:
Here a **closed surface** $S$ means a nonempty, compact, connected, boundaryless topological $2$-manifold in the convention of the earlier definition *Topological manifolds with and without boundary*: $S$ is Hausdorff (distinct points have disjoint open neighborhoods), has an at-most-countable basis of open sets (every open set is a union of basis members), and for every $x\in S$ there are an open neighborhood $U$ and a homeomorphism $h:U\to V$ onto an open subset $V\subseteq\mathbb R^2_+$, where $\mathbb R^2_+=\{(t_1,t_2)\in\mathbb R^2:t_2\ge0\}$. The model boundary is $t_2=0$, and the manifold boundary subset defined by that chart convention is empty; equivalently, every point has a neighborhood homeomorphic to an open subset of $\mathbb R^2$. It is **orientable** when it has an $R$-orientation for $R=\mathbb Z$ under the earlier definition *R-orientation of a topological manifold*: a continuous section of the local homology system with fibers $H_2(S,S\setminus\{x\};\mathbb Z)$ that generates each fiber.

A finite cellulation $K$ of $S$ is a finite $2$-dimensional CW decomposition whose open $2$-cells are disks. Write $V,E,F$ for its finite vertex, edge, and face sets. The primal graph has vertices $V$ and edges $E$. The dual graph has one vertex for each face and one dual edge crossing each primal edge, joining the two incident face sides; loops and multiple edges are allowed. Assume both graphs are connected. Let $\mathbb F_2=\{0,1\}$ with addition modulo two. Incidence multiplicities are reduced modulo two: $\partial_1:\mathbb F_2^E\to\mathbb F_2^V$ sends each edge to the sum of its endpoint incidences, and $\partial_2:\mathbb F_2^F\to\mathbb F_2^E$ sends each face to its boundary-edge incidence vector. These cellular boundary maps satisfy $\partial_1\partial_2=0$. Since $S$ has no boundary, each edge has two incident face sides, counted with multiplicity, so $\partial_2(\sum_{f\in F}f)=0$.

Identify $E$ with a finite region $\Lambda\subset\mathbb Z$ and use the finite local spin matrix algebra on $\Lambda$ with spin dimension $q=2$. The edge Hilbert space is $\mathcal H_K=(\mathbb C^2)^{\otimes E}$, so $\dim\mathcal H_K=2^{|E|}$. Let $X=\begin{pmatrix}0&1\\1&0\end{pmatrix}$ and $Z=\begin{pmatrix}1&0\\0&-1\end{pmatrix}$. For $a,b\in\mathbb F_2^E$, define $X(a)=\bigotimes_{e\in E}X^{a_e}$, $Z(b)=\bigotimes_{e\in E}Z^{b_e}$, and $P(a,b)=X(a)Z(b)$. For a vertex $v$ and face $f$, put $A_v=X(\partial_1^T v)$ and $B_f=Z(\partial_2 f)$, where $v$ and $f$ also denote the corresponding basis vectors. Thus $A_v$ is the product of $X$ over incident edges with odd incidence, and $B_f$ is the product of $Z$ over boundary edges with odd incidence. The identity $\partial_1\partial_2=0$ makes every $A_v$ commute with every $B_f$; each is a self-adjoint involution.

For positive real coefficients $J_v,K_f$, define the toric-code Hamiltonian

$$H_K=\sum_{v\in V}J_v\frac{I-A_v}{2}+\sum_{f\in F}K_f\frac{I-B_f}{2}.$$

The Pauli operators are dimensionless. In a physical interpretation, $J_v,K_f$ have energy units (joules in SI); here they are positive mathematical coefficients and no measured values are asserted. A simultaneous $+1$ eigenvector of all $A_v,B_f$ is called a ground vector. The ground space is their common $+1$ eigenspace, equivalently $\ker H_K$.

For the square $L\times L$ torus, $L\ge3$, use vertices $\mathbb Z_L^2$, horizontal and vertical nearest-neighbor edges, and the $L^2$ square faces, with periodic boundary conditions. A coordinate cycle is a closed edge path winding once around one coordinate direction. Let $p_1,p_2$ be the horizontal and vertical coordinate cycles in the primal graph, and let $q_1,q_2$ be the corresponding vertical and horizontal coordinate cycles in the dual graph, chosen so that $I(p_i,q_j)=\delta_{ij}$. The mod-two intersection number is the parity of primal edges crossed by a dual cycle. A topological disk is a subset homeomorphic to the closed unit disk. A finite edge support is disk-local with full complement cycles if it is contained in a topological disk whose complement contains representatives of these two primal and two dual coordinate cycles. The phrase “both independent homology cycles” below refers to these two primal cycles and their dual crossing representatives.

An open primal path is a path in the vertex-edge graph; its $Z$ string is $Z(b)$ for its edge chain $b$. An open dual path is a path in the face-adjacency graph; its $X$ string is $X(a)$ for the primal edges crossed by that dual path. A closed string has zero endpoint boundary in the corresponding primal or dual graph. The support of an operator is a finite edge set $S$ such that the operator is a matrix on $(\mathbb C^2)^{\otimes S}$ tensored with the identity on $E\setminus S$.

items.title: Commuting stabilizers and topological degeneracy
items.physical_scope: Pure finite-dimensional mathematics for the stated unperturbed Hamiltonian; no empirical realization or perturbation stability claim.
items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $K$ be a finite cellulation of a closed, connected, orientable surface of genus $g\ge0$, with the incidence and Hamiltonian conventions of the toric-code definition. For positive couplings $J_v,K_f$, the Hamiltonian is positive and frustration free, meaning its positive penalty terms have a common zero vector. Its ground-space dimension is $2^{2g}$. Define its spectral gap as the least positive eigenvalue of $H_K$, or $+\infty$ if there is no positive eigenvalue. This gap is at least $2m$, where $m=\min(\{J_v:v\in V\}\cup\{K_f:f\in F\})>0$, and in particular is at least $m$. On a uniform $L\times L$ square torus with $L\ge3$ and couplings $J_v=J>0$, $K_f=K>0$, the exact gap is $2\min(J,K)$.

items.title: Disk-supported Pauli centralizers are stabilizers
items.physical_scope: Pure finite-dimensional mathematics on the unperturbed square-torus stabilizer model; no perturbation stability claim.
items.statement: Let $K_L$ be the square $L\times L$ torus cellulation with $L\ge3$. For $a,b\in\mathbb F_2^E$, let $P(a,b)=X(a)Z(b)$, where $X(a)=\bigotimes_eX^{a_e}$ and $Z(b)=\bigotimes_eZ^{b_e}$. Suppose its edge support is contained in a disk whose complement contains primal cycles $p_1,p_2$ and dual cycles $q_1,q_2$ with $I(p_i,q_j)=\delta_{ij}$. Write $A_v=X(\partial_1^Tv)$ and $B_f=Z(\partial_2f)$. If $P(a,b)$ commutes with every $A_v$ and $B_f$, then there are vertex and face chains $u\in\mathbb F_2^V$ and $w\in\mathbb F_2^F$ such that $a=\partial_1^Tu$ and $b=\partial_2w$. Consequently $P(a,b)$ is a product of the vertex and face stabilizers.

items.title: Crossing strings and local scalar compression
items.physical_scope: Exact finite square-torus stabilizer algebra only; no perturbation-stability or thermodynamic-limit claim.
items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice and use the square $L\times L$ torus cellulation, $L\ge3$. A closed primal $Z$ string and a closed dual $X$ string commute or anticommute according to the parity of their edge crossings: their commutator sign is $(-1)^{I}$, where $I$ is the mod-two intersection number. Let $P_0$ be the orthogonal projection onto the common $+1$ eigenspace of all vertex and face stabilizers. For any operator $O$ supported on an edge set contained in a disk whose complement contains the coordinate cycles $p_1,p_2,q_1,q_2$ specified in the definition, there is a scalar $\lambda(O)\in\mathbb C$ such that $P_0OP_0=\lambda(O)P_0$. This is exact local indistinguishability for the unperturbed finite Hamiltonian.

title: Toric-code Hamiltonians and local indistinguishability — Examples

items.title: Open strings create endpoint defects
items.physical_scope: Finite-dimensional example in the exact unperturbed toric-code Hamiltonian; no empirical or perturbative claim.
items.statement: On a finite connected toric-code cellulation, let $\gamma$ be a primal path that visits no vertex twice and has distinct endpoint vertices $v_1,v_2$, and let $\gamma^*$ be a dual path that visits no face twice and has distinct endpoint faces $f_1,f_2$. Acting on any ground vector, the $Z$ string along $\gamma$ flips exactly the endpoint eigenvalues $A_{v_1},A_{v_2}$ and raises the energy by $J_{v_1}+J_{v_2}$. The $X$ string along $\gamma^*$ flips exactly $B_{f_1},B_{f_2}$ and raises the energy by $K_{f_1}+K_{f_2}$.
